content: Rectified spirit, also known as rectified alcohol, is a highly concentrated form of ethanol that has undergone purification through a process called rectification, which involves repeated distillation. This type of alcohol is utilized for various purposes, including medicinal applications, as a household solvent, and as an ingredient in mixed alcoholic beverages. Rectified spirits can be derived from different plant materials, with common sources being sugar beets and potatoes. Neutral grain spirits, a subset of rectified spirits, are specifically produced from grains. In the United States, a rectified spirit branded as Spirytus Stawski is imported from Poland by Stawski Imports, based in Chicago, Illinois. This product contains 96% alcohol by volume (192 proof) and is also available in a 76% alcohol variant (152 proof). It is characterized by its colorless, tasteless, and nearly odorless properties. Another well-known rectified spirit in the U.S. is Everclear, which is bottled by Luxco. Everclear is available in strengths of up to 95% alcohol (190 proof), although some states have prohibited the sale of the 190-proof version. In Poland, rectified spirit is referred to as spirytus rektyfikowany. The Polish version is distilled to slightly above 95% alcohol (190 proof). While tourists in Poland are allowed to purchase and consume spirytus, exporting it is prohibited by law. However, enforcement of this export restriction is relatively lenient. In Germany, rectified spirit is commonly known as Primasprit in colloquial terms or Neutralalkohol in more technical language. German rectified spirit is typically distilled to 96.5% alcohol (193 proof). It is primarily used for the preparation of homemade liqueurs, with other applications being uncommon. Most of the Primasprit produced in Germany is derived from grain, making it a neutral grain spirit.
